cosy-lesson.title: Living with Family vs Living Alone (B1)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Independence ≠ reliance – freedom from outside control or support.

p.em: Example: Living alone fosters rapid personal independence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Privacy ≠ exposure – the state of being free from public attention or intrusion.

p.em: Example: Privacy is one of the main advantages of having one's own apartment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Companionship ≠ loneliness – a feeling of fellowship or friendship.

p.em: Example: Living with family provides constant companionship.

cosy-blockquote.p: Household chores ≠ leisure – routine domestic tasks like cooking and cleaning.

p.em: Example: Sharing household chores reduces individual workload.

cosy-blockquote.p: Solitude ≠ isolation – the state of being alone without feeling lonely.

p.em: Example: Enjoying solitude allows for reflection and study.

cosy-blockquote.p: Financial burden ≠ savings – heavy cost or financial pressure.

p.em: Example: Renting alone can create a heavy financial burden.

cosy-blockquote.p: Autonomy ≠ restriction – the right or condition of self-government.

p.em: Example: Personal autonomy lets you design your home environment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Support network ≠ solo – a group of people who provide practical and emotional help.

p.em: Example: Family offers an immediate support network during illness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boundaries ≠ conflict – rules that establish personal space and privacy.

p.em: Example: Clear boundaries prevent conflicts between family members.

cosy-blockquote.p: Adaptability ≠ rigidity – the quality of being able to adjust to new conditions.

p.em: Example: Living with others requires daily compromise and adaptability.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does living independently foster personal autonomy and self-reliance?
★ At what point in life did you feel completely independent?

What strategies help maintain personal privacy when sharing an apartment?
★ How do you establish boundaries with family or flatmates?

Why is emotional companionship vital when transitioning to adulthood?
★ Do you rely on family or close friends for emotional support?

How should adults divide daily household chores to prevent resentment?
★ What is your least favorite domestic task?

What is the difference between enjoying peaceful solitude and feeling lonely?
★ How do you recharge your energy after a busy week?

How can young professionals manage the heavy financial burden of solo housing?
★ What portion of your monthly income goes toward housing?

How does living with relatives impact a young person's daily support network?
★ How close are you to your extended family?

Why is setting clear personal boundaries essential for harmonious living?
★ Have you ever had a disagreement with a roommate over boundaries?

How does domestic adaptability prepare individuals for future relationship challenges?
★ How easily do you adapt to other people's living habits?

How does personal independence shape a person's career choices and identity?
★ Do you prefer making major life choices entirely on your own?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Personal autonomy is impossible to achieve while living under your parents' roof. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Did living at home limit your freedom as a young adult?

Protecting your personal privacy is more difficult in a family household than in solo living. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Value privacy or constant social connection more?

Constant companionship at home reduces stress and prevents depression. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Does coming home to an empty apartment feel peaceful or lonely?

Splitting household chores strictly fifty-fifty is essential for domestic harmony. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you negotiate household responsibilities?

Embracing regular solitude leads to greater self-awareness and emotional maturity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you actively schedule solo time during the week?

The heavy financial burden of living alone outweighs the benefit of absolute freedom. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you compromise on space to save money?

A strong family support network provides a safety net that solo living cannot match. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How often do you consult your family about financial matters?

Establishing healthy boundaries with relatives becomes easier after moving out. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Has moving out improved your relationship with your family?

Domestic adaptability is a key indicator of long-term relationship success. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How flexible are you when sharing space?

Full financial independence should be achieved before moving into one's own place. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Is moving out early worth taking financial risks?

ul.li: Incorrect: Living alone is more better for independence. → Correct: Living alone is much better for independence. ((Do not double comparatives: use 'much better', not 'more better'.))
Incorrect: I am living alone since three years. → Correct: I have been living alone for three years. ((Use present perfect + 'for' for ongoing duration.))
